prompt:
Task: HD remaster of a sheet of animation frames from the 1995 adventure game The Dig (LucasArts), in the smooth, detailed style approved for the main characters. This is a production asset. Every frame is fitted to the original frame's size and position afterwards, and the game lays it over the HD background with its own soft edges.

Input: the attached image is the original low-resolution sheet enlarged 4x with hard pixel edges. The frames stand apart on a plain flat cyan background (#00C8C8). Around the sheet is a plain gray (#808080) border. The border is only padding.

All frames on this sheet are animation frames of the same character (Ludger Brink), in different poses. On this sheet, row by row from left to right: start pose, facing right (1 frame); animation 7, facing right (16 frames).

Do:
- Repaint every frame in high resolution with clean, natural detail: smooth shading instead of dithering, smooth anti-aliased outlines (no pixel steps), believable cloth, skin, hair and material.
- Keep the original look: the same character, the same colors, light direction, shadows and contrast, in the painted style of the approved HD sheets.
- Make all frames look identical apart from the pose: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and light in every frame. The frames are played one after another in the game, so any difference between them flickers.
- Keep the pose, proportions and silhouette of every frame as in the input, and keep each frame in its place on the sheet, in the same rows and the same order.
- Glowing effects (light, energy, lightning, sparks) are painted as soft glow that fades into transparency.

Do not:
- Do not add, remove, merge or redesign frames. Do not add anything between the frames: no shadows, floor, text, numbers, labels, frames or grid lines.
- Do not let frames touch or overlap each other.
- Some frames show only part of the character, for example a body without a head or a head alone, because the game draws the parts separately. Paint them as they are and do not complete them.
- Small bright magenta marks under the feet or at the edges are shadow markers used by the game. Leave them out; the game draws the shadow itself.
- No photorealism, no modern 3D look, no film grain, no vignette, no watermark, no signature.

Output: one PNG image, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, with a fully transparent background (real alpha, no background color and no gray border) and the frames in the same layout as the input. List the delivery with its sha256 in the fremdrift.json of your report and add a rutekart (the box around each frame's drawing) as for the main characters.

If a second image is attached, it is an already approved HD sheet of the same character, or an approved HD picture from the same game. Paint the character exactly as in that image: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and level of detail. Take all poses and the layout from the first image.


TOM-AUTHORIZED SOURCE VARIANT AND BRINK STYLE CORRECTION, 10 OCTOBER 2026:
Image ONE is the actual original source animation sheet, authority for every exact pose, angle, silhouette, animation phase, costume, source lighting, palette and row order. Image TWO is Tom's approved Brink face crop, ONLY his lean angular scientist identity, long straight nose, narrow tapered chin, neat hair shape and clean smooth2D drawn rendering. Do NOT copy the warm pink skin or normal blond color of this healthy face anchor. Image THREE is the factual originalRGBA count/ID guide of this output sheet; no gray or labels in output. Image FOUR is a nearest-neighbor enlargement of the ACTUAL first original head of costume173, not a creative recolor: this controls the real GREEN-LIGHT skin/hair/jacket palette. Paint the smooth approved drawn identity UNDER THE EXACT ORIGINAL GREEN LIGHT. Actual source clothes/colors always win over a healthy face model.

THIS VARIANT IS BRINK IN GREEN LIGHT, with visibly dark olive/sallow source skin and green-olive illuminated straw hair. It is not the ordinary pink healthy palette and not Boston/Maggie. Keep the original variant light on every frame, even while face/mouth/body angle changes. Dark muted olive facial planes, not warm peach/tan/orange/pink skin. Hair muted yellow-green/olive as source, not bright normal golden blond. This is precisely the source variant, not permission to invent damage, glowing eyes, tears or a new character.
ACTUAL SOURCE PALETTE from costume173_000 RGBA: skin lit #8B7F3F (139,127,63), mid #6F5F2B (111,95,43), shade #57471F (87,71,31), deep #3B2F13 (59,47,19). Hair lit #97AF2F (151,175,47), dark #636F1F (99,111,31). Jacket green-gray #5F8773 (95,135,115), #3F675F (63,103,95), #27474B (39,71,75). Trousers DARK olive-brown/rust #5F3307 (95,51,7), shade #4B2300 (75,35,0), restrained highlight #733F00 (115,63,0). Very dark navy undershirt #13232F (19,35,47), boots #070B13 (7,11,19), source chest patch very dark blue #000063 ONLY where source actually visible. Preserve that dark brown pant family, not ordinary bright#BB4700/#8F2F00 orange-rust. Smooth antialiasing/highlights can interpolate inside these source hue families; never relight into healthy warm skin, gray-gray jacket, lemon/gold hair or fluorescent orange trousers. No gray healthy-palette backdrop from the face crop.

Keep slim angular scientist proportions, no broad muscular superhero torso, square action-hero jaw, short blunt nose, round inflated plastic face, furry/textured hair or photoreal rendering. Clean2D hand-drawn adventure animation, confident dark contours, angular drawn shadow planes with restrained smooth transitions. Clothing is the exact source open jacket, dark shirt, source small blue patch, plain brown trousers and dark boots. Retain tiny authentic source thigh detail only where actually visible; no new cargo pockets, pouches, panels, stripes, gear or decoration. Hands are empty, no green crystal/weapon/prop is present on this sheet.

Each source unit is separate. Keep the exact foot/arm/knee pose and facing direction of every frame; do not clone one pose over different originals. Talking phases change mouth/jaw only, retaining stable skull/hairline/eyes/ears/nose/neck attachment and body scale. All back/back-three-quarter views show back of hair and ear where visible, never a front eye/brow/nose/mouth. Source bright MAGENTA at ground/feet is a technical shadow marker: OMIT it entirely without a new cast shadow, ground or pink boots. Keep all actual dark boot portions and source shape, never add a body part merely to replace a magenta patch.

Exactly1536x1024 nativeRGBA PNG fully transparent outside the exact drawings. No cyan/gray padding, palette cards, labels, numbers, grid, floor/cast shadows, vignette, colored haze/halo field, stray pixels or magenta markers. Antialias only immediately along the source contours, no low-opacity atmospheric backdrop between units. No creative postprocessing.


EXACT SHEET173_01: THREE rows [1,8,8], exactly17 FULL-BODY Brink drawings, no tiny fragmentfallback.
Top row exactly1:source000, the original leaning-back/sideways standing pose, head angled in the precise source near-front/three-quarter direction, one shoulder raised, one arm low, exact bent-knee stance and two original dark boots. Full body, no removed feet.
Second row exactly8:074/060/039/034/033/006/032/031. All maintain the source same leaning standing body and exact source balance/hand/foot positions, with distinct source mouth/brow/head phases. Keep every own mouth opening/closing rather than one cloned face. Leaning torso/knees must match source, not straight neutral standing.
Third row exactly8:030/029/028/024/016/015/014/013, continuing exact source talking phases in same leaning standing body. No arm/knee/foot sequence invented. One person per source unit, no doubled heads, no head-only units, no reconstructed missing body.
The source shoulder/arm tilt and asymmetrical bent legs are deliberate, not perspective error to normalize. Keep all17 same natural skull size, neck attachment and costume palette; only prescribed source mouth/pose states vary. Source layout/gaps from imageONE, not a new centered character gallery.
